title: TRPs as tools and in the gut
objective: Evaluate how TRP channels are used to target or manipulate neurons, and the caveats of each approach.

steps.title: Three ways labs use TRPV1
steps.body:
- **Genetic access:** `Trpv1-Cre` mice drive reporters, [[DREADD|DREADDs]] or other payloads in TRPV1-lineage neurons.
- **Pharmacology:** TRPV1 agonists or antagonists probe the channel's role in a behavior.
- **Marker:** TRPV1 expression helps identify a subset of [[nociceptor|nociceptors]].

steps.title: The lineage caveat
steps.body:
A Cre line marks every cell that **ever** expressed the gene, including during development. `Trpv1` is expressed broadly in developing [[DRG]] neurons, so `Trpv1-Cre` can mark **many more** neurons than express TRPV1 in the adult.

The fix: check the marked population ([[RNAscope]], C8), or use a [[CreER]] (C2) or an [[intersectional genetics|intersectional]] strategy (C3).

flag.note: How broadly Trpv1-Cre marks neurons depends on the specific line and reporter; check the characterization for the line you use.

visual.alt: Two columns of the same DRG neurons. In development, three express Trpv1 and are permanently marked by Trpv1-Cre (a star). In the adult only one still expresses TRPV1, yet three still carry the reporter, so reporter-positive exceeds TRPV1-positive.
visual.caption: A Cre line marks every cell that ever expressed the gene, not just those expressing it now.

steps.prompt: A paper says it used `Trpv1-Cre` with hM4Di to quiet TRPV1 neurons. What's your first question?
options: What fluorescent color was chosen for the reporter protein?
In adults, which neurons does the line actually mark?
How many years of experience did the authors have with mice?
What solvent was the actuator dissolved in before injection?
steps.explanation: Lineage marking can widen the targeted population far beyond adult TRPV1-positive neurons, which changes how you read the result (C2 logic).

variants.setup: A paper silences 'TRPV1 neurons' using Trpv1-Cre with hM4Di.
variants.prompt: What should you check first before trusting the targeting?
options: Which fluorophore the reporter used, and how bright it was
Which neurons the line marks in adults vs. its developmental lineage
How many years the authors have worked with mice
Which solvent the actuator was dissolved in
variants.reveal: Trpv1-Cre marks the developmental lineage, often broader than adult TRPV1⁺ cells — verify with RNAscope, CreER, or an intersection.

steps.title: TRPV1 neurons and the gut
steps.body: TRPV1-positive afferents richly innervate the gut. The 2025 review of spinal gut innervation notes that chemogenetically quieting TRPV1-positive neurons lowers inflammation-driven visceral hypersensitivity. That is one reason [[DREADD|DREADDs]] are an accepted tool in this subfield, and part of the rationale for your pancreas project.

flag.note: The exact afferent subtypes and organs involved vary; see the review and primary papers.

steps.setup: You plan to use a Cre line to express a DREADD in a 'TRPV1' population and study the pancreas.
steps.prompt: Name one specificity check you'd run before trusting the targeting.
steps.reveal: Options: RNAscope or antibody staining to see which cells carry the reporter in the adult pancreas-projecting population; a CreER line with timed tamoxifen to avoid developmental lineage; an intersectional Cre+Flp design to restrict to the subtype you want; retrograde labeling from the pancreas to confirm the marked cells actually project there. Any one shows you're testing the neurons you think you are.

sources.note: Review of spinal (DRG) sensory innervation of the intestine and open questions.

reviewNotes: Confidence medium: lineage breadth and subtype specifics flagged. Links to C2/C3/C8 and capstone.
